core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 3269-3290): over the maximal isomorphism open the cokernel f_*O_{X'}/O_X is a direct sum of skyscraper sheaves Q_i of finite O_{X,x_i}-length; the induction runs on the total length of the cokernel, considering factorizations X' -> Y -> X with O_X subset g_*O_Y subset f_*O_{X'}.
Several singular points (proof lines 3292-3296): if n > 1, the inverse image of Q_1 inside f_*O_{X'} defines an O_X-subalgebra giving a nontrivial factorization, and induction wins.

One singular point (proof lines 3298-3313): for A = O_{X,x} inside B = (f_*O_{X'})_x, the chain A subset A + m_A B subset B either splits (induction) or A + m_A B = B, which by Nakayama forces A = B when both inclusions are strict, leaving the essential case B = A + m_A B.

Terminal classification (proof lines 3313-3321): C = B/m_A B has at most two k-subalgebras, hence exactly two, so C = k x k or C = k[epsilon] by lemma-no-in-between-over-k, corresponding exactly to the glueing of two points and the squishing of a tangent vector.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the cokernel into finite-length skyscraper sheaves and set up induction on total length over intermediate subalgebras.
Split off points one at a time when more than one singular point remains.
At a single point use the algebra chain A subset A + m_A B subset B and Nakayama to isolate the essential extension.
Classify the terminal case by the two-subalgebra dichotomy and identify the two modification types.
difficulty_reason: The lemma factors any finite almost-isomorphism into the two elementary modifications (statement lines 3257-3267). The proof (lines 3269-3321) is a complete induction on the length of the cokernel: skyscraper decomposition, the multi-point splitting step, the single-point algebra chain with the Nakayama dichotomy, and the terminal classification via the exactly-two-subalgebras lemma. Every step is present with no omitted details. H2: a systematic induction with correctly ordered hinges, each short.
